title: gates/<gate_id>.json - one send that waits for a person
description: runs/<id>/gates/<gate_id>.json, written by src/gate.js (requestGate, answerGate) with a temp file, fsync and rename. It is a view: the record is runs/<id>/gate-ledger.jsonl (schemas/gate-ledger-v1.json). A gate is approved only when a ledger that verifies holds a gate_answered line from a person's channel for this gate's sha256, and the text file still hashes to it; a gate file that says 'approved' on its own approves nothing. 'expired' is derived from expires_at when the gate is read and never written here; an approval is usable for a send only until expires_at and only once.

id.description: g<n>: the n-th gate this run requested, counted in the ledger.

kind.description: What the gate approves, chosen by the server (an advice send is 'advice'); never a tool argument.

status.description: As last written. When the ledger holds an answer and this file still says pending with no answer (a crash between the two writes), the ledger wins; any other disagreement makes the gate read invalid.

text.description: The text file the person approves, relative to the run folder, '/'-separated. requestGate refuses a path outside the run folder or a link that leads out of it, and every read of the text checks the same again, so a forged path reads as unreadable.

sha256.description: sha256 of the text file's raw bytes when the gate was requested.

bytes.description: The text file's size in bytes when the gate was requested.

price.description: What the send could cost, as the caller priced it (an advice gate: ceiling_usd and expected_usd). null when not given.

seats.description: Who the text would go to, as the caller described them (an advice gate: lab, model, retention wording).

sensitivity.description: The effective sensitivity label and who set it, as the caller gave them. null when not given.

follow_up.description: Present only when the send follows an advisor's request for more material (0.8.1 DR-8): the line the person is shown about it. Bound by meta_sha256 when present; absent, the hash is as before.

masks.description: How many values of each kind were masked in the text before the gate was requested.

meta_sha256.description: sha256 of the canonical JSON (keys sorted at every depth) of price, seats, sensitivity, masks and follow_up (when present), also on the gate_requested ledger line: an edit of any of them in this file makes the gate read invalid.

expires_at.description: After this the gate reads 'expired' and cannot be answered. Default ten minutes after the request, the life of a council_quote.

seq.description: The ledger line that requested this gate.

answer.description: null while pending; the answer as the ledger records it once answered.

channel.description: A channel a person uses (PERSON_CHANNELS in src/gate.js).

actor.description: Who answered, as the channel knows it (the CLI: the OS user name).

tty.description: true when the CLI saw a terminal on stdin and stdout. Friction, not proof of a person: a pseudo-terminal passes.

seq.description: The ledger line that holds this answer.
